messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: PyStan
parts:
Stan is written in C++ and can be run from the command line and from R. We’d like for Python users to be able to run Stan as well. If anyone is interested in doing this, please let us know and we’d be happy to work with you on it!

Andrew

messages.author: a7da442f3527310e
messages.subject: Re: PyStan
parts:
I've used python to run Stan for a recently-submitted paper. Since I was just trying to get my experiments run, after a few minutes of establishing that it'd be a nontrivial amount of work to write a python interface directly, I instead wrote an interface to use RStan through python (via the rpy2 bridge): https://gist.github.com/dougalsutherland/5093571.

This worked okay for me and may be useful to others, though it feels a little silly and certainly complicates the toolchain to add R into the mix. All this code lets you do is compile models with stan_model() and then extract() the results of sampling() from it, though that's just because that's all I needed; it shouldn't be hard to wrap any of the other R functions. It also currently caches compiled models by pickling the rpy2 object; it might be preferable to save and load models in R-land, but as someone who's never used R before I was having trouble getting that to work and opted for the zero-effort solution instead.


I looked briefly into the possibility of writing an interface to the sampler model, but didn't want to go through the work of writing a stan::io::var_context implementation and so on. Also, Python's C++ interoperability isn't great; AFAIK your options are
  • write C wrappers to your C++ API and then call them through ctypes, Cython, etc
  • use Boost::Python, which I've attempted to learn and found to be an enormous chore due mainly to the crazy build system they insist on using
  • use Cython's C++ support, which isn't especially well-documented and I had troubles with when I last attempted it a year ago
  • use the Python C APIs manually, which is presumably not that hard but I've never tried.
I'd be happy to work on a real, direct Python interface to Stan. I wonder if the best approach might not be, though, to first make an easy-to-use C wrapper for compiled Stan models. This would make Stan easier to wrap for Python and other languages that have good C interaction but nothing like RCpp with such good C++ interaction.

- Dougal

I could help with a python interface but probably not until April sometime.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: PyStan
parts:
Thanks -- you're the third person to jump in and
volunteer, so now we have to sort out our options.
We don't want to run a competition :-)

We definitely don't want to do Python through RStan.
It's just too messy.

For the other options, I don't know them that well,
but indeed, Boost.Python is not just a header-only lib
like the rest of the things in Boost we use.

- Bob
